conclusion: The 80-epoch equal-weight run was worse for different reasons by environment: TwoRoom exported a final checkpoint after late validation collapse, while PushT improved supervised validation loss but lost high-K planner utility.

pusht.cause: high-K planner/objective mismatch, not ordinary validation-loss overtraining

experiment_design_caveats.not_a_clean_continuation: Changing schedule.max_epochs from 10 to 80 also stretches LinearWarmupCosineAnnealingLR because total_steps=max_epochs*len(train_loader).
experiment_design_caveats.checkpoint_selection: Training used ModelCheckpoint(save_last=True, save_top_k=0), so best validation checkpoints were not retained.
experiment_design_caveats.checkpoint_cadence_changed: Equal-long configs changed checkpoint_every_n_train_steps from 1000 to 5000.

next_actions: Do not rerun equal-weight 80 epochs as-is.
For long training, save and export best checkpoints on a high-K-aware validation metric.
For a true continuation test, keep 10-epoch LR schedule semantics or resume from the 10-epoch checkpoint with an explicit continuation schedule.
Proceed with high-K-weighted training configs because PushT failure is localized to high-K planner utility.
